title: Teen Scientists Get to Use a Giant Particle Smasher!
summary:
What would you do if you got to use one of the most powerful machines on Earth? Six high school students from India got to do just that! They won a competition called Beamline for Schools, which lets students design and run experiments using particle accelerators — giant machines that smash tiny particles together to learn about the universe.

The team, called attoPION, beat out 712 teams from 89 countries. That's a lot of competition! They worked with Manu Srivastava, a graduate student at MIT, who helped them turn their idea into a real experiment.

Their experiment is about pions, which are tiny particles that live for a very short time. They wanted to see what happens when a pion hits a neutron (another tiny particle). This might sound super complicated, but it's important for a big experiment called DUNE, which studies neutrinos — particles that are so tiny they can pass through almost anything.

At CERN, the students spent two weeks building and running their experiment. They used detectors and computers to collect data. They even got to attend talks by real CERN scientists!

The experiment was really hard because the thing they were looking for is super rare. But the students worked together and learned what it's like to be a scientist. Srivastava said the students were 'very genuine' and really wanted to do something nice.

This is a great example of how kids can do amazing things when they work hard and get a little help. Who knows? Maybe one day, you could design an experiment at CERN too!
why_it_matters: It shows that kids can do real science when they work hard, and that science is for everyone, not just grown-ups in labs.
